text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- Bank of Spain lowers government's optimistic economic forecasts.
- ETA murders army officer in Madrid with same gun used in attack on two generals.
- Juan Ortiz Urculo manages to expel High Court chief prosecutor.
EL MUNDO
- Driver of murdered army officer identifies Ainhoa Mugica as one of attackers.
- Army officer's widow asks government to be harder on ETA.
- Civil Guard removes parot from exhibit at Reina Sofia at request of ecologists.
DIARIO 16
- Policeman Jose Amedo says Pedro Jose Ramirez acted on orders of High Court jugde Baltasar Garzon.
ABC
- Widow of army officer shot dead in attack on Wednesday responds to ETA with serenity.
CINCO DIAS

- Telefonica, bathing in glory of surging shares prices, positive analyst reports, glowing results, plans to launch 196.7 million shares, according to market sources, still held by the state on January 20.
- BBV employees will receive bonus in shares priced at 3,000 pesetas each.
- Labour reform of 1994 permitted rise of three points in 1995 of variable part of workers salary.
EXPANSION
- Telefonica prompts another record high turnover on Spanish bourse.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Juan Miguel Villar Mir does not come up with sufficient backing to ensure government credit, through ICO, of 5 billion pesetas for construction firm Huarte.
- Government modifies concession of aid to protected housing.
- Caja Madrid converts its subsidary Altae into bank for rich.
